plan.title: Alan Turing: The Man Who Taught Machines to Think
plan.description: A short profile of Alan Turing, the British mathematician who helped break wartime codes and asked whether machines can think. Learn why his ideas still shape every computer we use.

beats.narration: He helped end a war, invented the idea of the modern computer, and asked if machines could think. Yet Alan Turing was barely honored in his own lifetime. Who was he?

Turing was a British mathematician. He imagined a simple abstract machine that could follow instructions to solve any problem that can be written as steps. That idea became the blueprint for computers.

During the Second World War, he worked with a team of codebreakers in Britain. They cracked secret enemy messages, using clever mathematics and machines. Their work saved countless lives and is believed to have shortened the war.
Later, he asked a bold question: can a machine think? He proposed a test, where a person chats with an unseen partner and tries to guess if it is human. People still debate it today.

turns.speaker: Person
turns.text: Am I talking to a human or a machine?

turns.speaker: Unseen partner
turns.text: Why not ask me something and decide?

beats.narration: Turing's life ended too early, and he was treated unjustly by his own country. Today, we recognize him as a founder of computer science. Every phone in your pocket carries his idea.

props.text: Every computer you use carries Alan Turing's idea.
